verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior: the same order of validation, pricing, reserve, charge, commit and redeem, the same messages and statuses, and the same swallowed receipt failure. B adds ten characterization tests that it confirmed against the original code. They pin the call order, rollback, per-line tax rounding, VIP stacking, free shipping and receipt-failure handling, which protects this production refactor from future regressions. A's 20k-case side-by-side fuzz was thorough, but it lives outside the repo and leaves no lasting protection. B does add churn by moving refund_order to a new position for no reason.
a_issues: No tests added: the randomized equivalence check was thrown away, so the thin existing suite is all that guards future edits to this production code
Helper lists are typed as a bare `list` instead of `list[Item]`

b_issues: Moves refund_order above the helpers without need, which makes the diff noisier and harder to review

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep the computation order, error messages, status values and rollback behavior the same, so both look correct. A also adds ten characterization tests to the repository. They cover rollback logging, rejecting an invalid coupon before any stock is touched, per-line tax rounding and swallowing a receipt failure, which protects this production-critical refactor going forward. B only fuzzed the change once, outside the repo, and left no tests behind, and its `_complete_order` mixes committing the order with sending the receipt across seven parameters. A has some misleading test names and a slightly overstated report, but it is still the safer merge.
a_issues: `test_vip_customer_gets_five_percent_off_after_coupon` uses no coupon, so it does not check the coupon-then-VIP ordering that its name and the report claim.
`test_declined_payment_releases_stock_in_reverse_of_reserve` is misnamed: it uses a single item, and the code releases in reserve order, not reverse.
Moving `refund_order` above the helpers adds diff noise that the task does not need.
b_issues: No tests are added to the repository; the 20k-case fuzz verification was thrown away, so nothing protects this refactor going forward.
`_complete_order` takes seven parameters and mixes committing stock and redeeming the coupon with sending the receipt.
Uses a bare `list` instead of `list[Item]` for reserved items.
